office.title: Indiana State Representative
office.summary: Members of the Indiana House of Representatives write and vote on state laws as part of the Indiana General Assembly. The House has 100 members, each representing one district for a two-year term [1].
duties: Introduces and votes on state legislation as one of the two chambers of the Indiana General Assembly [1].
Must be at least 21 years old when taking office and have lived in the district for at least a year [1].

incumbent.name: Bob Behning
incumbent.summary: Bob Behning (Robert W. Behning on the ballot), a Republican from Indianapolis, has served in the Indiana House since 1992 and chairs the House Education Committee; he also serves on the Public Health Committee [3, 4]. The House Republican caucus says he authored the 2011 law creating Indiana's school voucher program and works at Marian University as director of its Center for Vibrant Schools [3].
record: December 2024: Reappointed chair of the House Education Committee; he said the committee would "continue our work to empower parents to send their students to the school of their choice" [4].
January 2025: In a column distributed by the caucus, urged moving the Choice Scholarship (voucher) program to universal eligibility by "eliminating the remaining income cap" [5].

April 2025: Voted for SB 1, the property-tax and local government finance bill, which passed the House 65–29 [6], and for the conference report on HEA 1001, the 2025–2027 state budget, adopted 66–27 [7].
May 2025: Authored HEA 1002, which the caucus says cut nearly 10% of the education code by removing outdated and duplicate provisions, unused programs and some pandemic-era mandates [8].
December 5, 2025: Voted for HB 1032, the mid-decade congressional redistricting bill, which passed the House 57–41 [9].
January 28, 2026: Voted for HB 1002, the electric utility affordability bill, which passed the House 89–4 [10].

2026 session: Authored HEA 1004, which the caucus says removed further outdated K-12 requirements and directs the State Board of Education to plan for career and technical education [11]. Authored HEA 1408, which the caucus says requires parental consent and monitoring tools for minors on social media and limits certain addictive features [12].

race_context: House District 91 covers a portion of Marion County, in central Indiana, according to the House Republican caucus [3].
Behning was re-elected in 2024 with 60.1% of the vote [13].
Behning and Hurt were each the only candidate listed in their party's May 5, 2026 primary [13].
No debate or forum between the candidates was found as of October 10, 2026; neither had answered Mirror Indy's voter-guide questions [14, 15].

Education is the main contrast: Behning authored the state's voucher program and has pushed universal eligibility, while Hurt's campaign calls for fully funding public schools, universal pre-K and free school lunch [3, 5, 16].

candidates.summary: Jarren Hurt, the Democratic nominee, is a Navy submarine veteran, real estate agent and owner of a fiber-optic installation business, according to his campaign [16].
background: His campaign describes him as a Navy submarine veteran, Eagle Scout and Indiana University graduate who works as a real estate agent and runs a utility fiber-optic installation company [16].
path_to_ballot: Was the only Democratic candidate listed for the May 5, 2026 primary [13].

items: Would fully fund public schools, support teachers, and back universal pre-K and free K-12 school lunch, according to his campaign [16].
Opposes subsidizing large technology companies at families' expense and would push back on data center projects that harm communities or the environment [16].
Supports cutting Indiana's gas tax and eliminating toll roads [16].
Would advocate for more affordable housing supply and keeping homeownership within reach [16].

on_incumbent: No statements by Hurt about Behning or his record were found on his campaign website or in voter guides [16, 15].
gaps: No news coverage, endorsements or campaign finance reports were found.
Hurt had not answered Mirror Indy's voter-guide questions as of Oct. 10, 2026.
Where he lives is not stated on his campaign site.

candidates.summary: Robert W. (Bob) Behning is the Republican incumbent, in the House since 1992, and chairs the House Education Committee [3].
background: Born and raised in Indianapolis; Indiana University graduate (1976); assistant vice president and director of the Center for Vibrant Schools at Marian University, according to the caucus [3].
path_to_ballot: Was the only Republican candidate listed for the May 5, 2026 primary [13].

items: Has advocated for universal private-school choice, writing that the program lets parents choose "regardless of income or ZIP code" [5], and has authored laws reducing state K-12 regulations; he said schools "should have the freedom to set their own requirements" [8, 11].
Said his 2026 social media law gives parents "more control over their children's social media use" [12].

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements by Behning about his challenger were found [3].
gaps: His campaign website (robertbehning.com) did not load; no 2026 campaign statements, endorsements or finance totals were found.
Behning had not answered Mirror Indy's voter-guide questions as of Oct. 10, 2026.

Which Marion County townships the district currently includes was not confirmed from a source read for this profile (older sources describe Decatur Township and parts of Hendricks and Morgan counties under pre-2021 maps).
The 2025 budget's change to voucher eligibility was not confirmed from a source read for this profile.
